name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent on *all* PRs—open and merged—for two weeks. This catches edge cases in routing and prompts without missing critical data. The trade-off is higher compute cost, but it’s temporary and safer than guessing which PRs matter.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent on *all* PRs risks drowning reviewers in noise—shadow mode already trains them to ignore autofeedback, so adding more will just dilute signal. Instead, run it on a random 20% sample of merged PRs for two weeks; if the hit rate of useful feedback matches PR-Agent’s claims, scale up. Settle it by comparing the ratio of actionable feedback to total PRs in both samples.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent only on PRs where the heuristic flags *both* new contributors *and* high churn in the changed files—this cuts compute by 80% while still catching the riskiest edge cases in routing and prompts. The trade-off is missing some edge cases, but the hit rate on critical data will stay high enough to validate the approach.
